hook: Did you know a mysterious dwarf planet candidate, 2026 ED138, is lurking beyond Pluto?

sections.voiceover: Did you know a mysterious dwarf planet candidate, 2026 ED138, is lurking beyond Pluto?
sections.visual_cue: Deep space starfield with a faint, distant moving light highlighted.

sections.voiceover: On October 27, 2026, the NSF-DOE Vera C. How does 2026 ED138 move through the dark, cold reaches of our solar system?
sections.visual_cue: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory building at night with data streams overlay.

sections.voiceover: But this object orbits the sun at 46 times the Earth-sun distance, tilted 25 degrees.
sections.visual_cue: Diagram showing the vast distance between the Sun and the object.

sections.voiceover: Mario Jurić at the University of Washington identified this unique path using Blanco 4-meter telescope data.
sections.visual_cue: Animation of an orbital path tilted 25 degrees relative to the solar plane.

sections.voiceover: Check the Minor Planet Center for more updates on the orbit of 2026 ED138.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the Milky Way galaxy seen from space.
